temperature.tooltip:
Temperature Sampler
• Function: Controls randomness and creativity in text generation by scaling the probability distribution over tokens
• Range: 0.0 to 2.0 (0.0 = completely deterministic, 1.0 = normal randomness, 2.0 = maximum creativity)
• Server Default: 0.8
• Effects: Lower values produce more focused/repetitive text, higher values increase diversity and unpredictability
• Sampler Name: 'temperature' (put in samplers array to activate)

top_k.tooltip:
Top-K Sampler
• Function: Limits token selection to the K most probable tokens, reducing low-probability choices
• Range: 0 to 1000 (0 = disabled, higher values = more token choices allowed)
• Server Default: 40
• Effects: Lower values focus generation on high-confidence words, higher values allow more vocabulary diversity
• Sampler Name: 'top_k' (put in samplers array to activate)

top_p.tooltip:
Top-P (Nucleus) Sampler
• Function: Selects tokens from smallest set that contains P probability mass, providing dynamic vocabulary control
• Range: 0.0 to 1.0 (higher values = larger token selection pool)
• Server Default: 0.9
• Effects: Lower values create more focused text, higher values allow broader vocabulary choices
• Sampler Name: 'top_p' (put in samplers array to activate)

min_p.tooltip:
Min-P Sampler
• Function: Sets minimum probability threshold relative to the most likely token, filtering out unlikely choices
• Range: 0.0 to 1.0 (0.0 = disabled, higher values = stricter filtering)
• Server Default: 0.1
• Effects: Higher values focus on high-confidence tokens, lower values allow more diverse but potentially incoherent choices
• Sampler Name: 'min_p' (put in samplers array to activate)

typical_p.tooltip:
Typical Sampler
• Function: Selects tokens with typical probability values, avoiding both overly predictable and overly surprising choices
• Range: 0.0 to 1.0 (1.0 = disabled, lower values = more typical selection)
• Server Default: 1.0 (disabled)
• Effects: Can produce more natural-sounding text by avoiding extreme probability values
• Sampler Name: 'typ_p' (put in samplers array to activate)

top_n_sigma.tooltip:
Top-N-Sigma Sampler
• Function: Statistical sampling that selects tokens based on their standard deviation from the mean probability
• Range: -1.0 to 2.0 (-1.0 = disabled, positive values = strictness level)
• Server Default: -1.0 (disabled)
• Effects: Lower values create more predictable text, higher values allow more statistical variation
• Sampler Name: 'top_n_sigma' (put in samplers array to activate)

mirostat.tooltip:
Mirostat Sampler
• Function: Advanced sampling method that maintains consistent text perplexity by adjusting tau parameter
• Range: 0, 1, or 2 (0 = disabled, 1 = Mirostat v1, 2 = Mirostat v2)
• Server Default: 0 (disabled)
• Effects: Produces more consistent text quality by maintaining target entropy levels
• WARNING: When enabled, overrides top-k, top-p, and typical sampling methods
• Sampler Name: 'mirostat' (put in samplers array to activate)

dry_multiplier.tooltip:
DRY Sampler (Main Control)
• Function: Advanced repetition penalty that penalizes sequences of repeated tokens rather than individual tokens
• Range: 0.0 to 5.0 (0.0 = disabled, higher values = stronger sequence penalty)
• Server Default: 0.0 (disabled)
• Effects: Reduces repetitive patterns in generated text while maintaining coherence better than simple repeat penalty
• Sampler Name: 'dry' (put in samplers array to activate)
• Requires: dry_base, dry_allowed_length, dry_penalty_last_n, dry_sequence_breakers parameters

xtc_probability.tooltip:
XTC Sampler (Main Control)
• Function: Probabilistically excludes the most likely tokens to increase text diversity and creativity
• Range: 0.0 to 1.0 (0.0 = disabled, higher values = more exclusion of top choices)
• Server Default: 0.0 (disabled)
• Effects: Can produce more creative and less predictable text by avoiding obvious token choices
• Sampler Name: 'xtc' (put in samplers array to activate)
• Requires: xtc_threshold parameter for optimal effectiveness

dynatemp_range.tooltip:
Dynamic Temperature Sampler (Main Control)
• Function: Dynamically adjusts temperature based on token probability entropy for adaptive randomness
• Range: 0.0 to 2.0 (0.0 = disabled, higher values = wider temperature variation)
• Server Default: 0.0 (disabled)
• Effects: Lower entropy contexts get lower temperature, higher entropy contexts get higher temperature
• Sampler Name: 'dynatemp' (put in samplers array to activate)
• Requires: dynatemp_exponent parameter for fine control

repeat_penalty.tooltip:
Penalties Sampler (Main Control)
• Function: Penalizes repeat sequences to reduce repetitive patterns
• Range: 0.0 to 2.0 (1.0 = no penalty, higher values = stronger anti-repetition)
• Server Default: 1.0 (disabled)
• Effects: Values above 1.0 discourage repetition, values below 1.0 encourage repetition
• WARNING: Too high values can break coherence and cause unnatural vocabulary choices
• Sampler Name: 'penalties' (put in samplers array to activate)
• Controls: repeat_penalty, frequency_penalty, presence_penalty, repeat_last_n, penalize_nl

frequency_penalty.tooltip:
Frequency Penalty (Penalties Sampler Parameter)
• Function: Penalizes tokens based on their frequency in the preceding text (linear scaling)
• Range: -2.0 to 2.0 (0.0 = no penalty, positive = discourage frequent tokens)
• Server Default: 0.0
• Effects: Higher values reduce repetition by penalizing frequently used tokens
• Controlled By: 'penalties' sampler (must be in samplers array)

presence_penalty.tooltip:
Presence Penalty (Penalties Sampler Parameter)
• Function: Penalizes tokens based on their presence in the preceding text (binary scaling)
• Range: -2.0 to 2.0 (0.0 = no penalty, positive = discourage repeated tokens)
• Server Default: 0.0
• Effects: Higher values encourage vocabulary diversity by penalizing any token that has already appeared
• Controlled By: 'penalties' sampler (must be in samplers array)

repeat_last_n.tooltip:
Repeat Last N Tokens (Penalties Sampler Parameter)
• Function: Number of recent tokens to consider when applying repeat penalty
• Range: -1 to 1000 (-1 = use full context, 0 = disable repeat penalty)
• Server Default: 64
• Effects: Larger values consider more history for repetition detection, smaller values focus on recent tokens
• Controlled By: 'penalties' sampler (must be in samplers array)

penalize_nl.tooltip:
Penalize Newlines (Penalties Sampler Parameter)
• Function: Whether to apply repeat penalty to newline characters
• Range: true or false
• Server Default: false
• Effects: true applies repeat penalty to newlines, false excludes them from repetition penalties
• Controlled By: 'penalties' sampler (must be in samplers array)

dry_base.tooltip:
DRY Sampling Base (DRY Sampler Parameter)
• Function: Base value for calculating DRY penalty strength, controls exponential scaling of sequence penalties
• Range: 1.0 to 4.0 (higher values = stronger exponential penalty growth)
• Server Default: 1.75
• Effects: Higher values create stronger penalties for longer repeated sequences
• Controlled By: 'dry' sampler (must be in samplers array and dry_multiplier > 0.0)

dry_allowed_length.tooltip:
DRY Allowed Length (DRY Sampler Parameter)
• Function: Minimum sequence length that is allowed to repeat without penalty
• Range: 0 to 10 (0 = penalize all repetitions, higher values = allow short repetitions)
• Server Default: 2
• Effects: Sequences shorter than this length can repeat freely, longer sequences get penalized
• Controlled By: 'dry' sampler (must be in samplers array and dry_multiplier > 0.0)

dry_penalty_last_n.tooltip:
DRY Penalty Last N (DRY Sampler Parameter)
• Function: Number of recent tokens to consider for DRY sequence repetition detection
• Range: -1 to 1000 (-1 = use full context, 0 = disable DRY)
• Server Default: -1 (full context)
• Effects: Larger values detect repetitions across more history, smaller values focus on recent patterns
• Controlled By: 'dry' sampler (must be in samplers array and dry_multiplier > 0.0)

dry_sequence_breakers.tooltip:
DRY Sequence Breakers (DRY Sampler Parameter)
• Function: Array of strings that break DRY sequence matching, preventing penalty across these boundaries
• Range: Array of strings (e.g., [\"\
\", \":\", \"\\\"\", \"*\"])
• Server Default: [\"\
\", \":\", \"\\\"\", \"*\"]
• Effects: Sequences are not considered repetitive if separated by these break characters
• Controlled By: 'dry' sampler (must be in samplers array and dry_multiplier > 0.0)

xtc_threshold.tooltip:
XTC Threshold (XTC Sampler Parameter)
• Function: Probability threshold for XTC (eXclude Top Choices) sampling, determines when to exclude top tokens
• Range: 0.0 to 1.0 (higher values = exclude fewer top choices)
• Server Default: 0.1
• Effects: Lower values exclude more top choices, increasing creativity but potentially reducing coherence
• Controlled By: 'xtc' sampler (must be in samplers array and xtc_probability > 0.0)

dynatemp_exponent.tooltip:
Dynamic Temperature Exponent (Dynamic Temperature Sampler Parameter)
• Function: Controls the curve shape for dynamic temperature adjustment based on entropy
• Range: 0.1 to 5.0 (1.0 = linear, higher = more aggressive adjustment)
• Server Default: 1.0
• Effects: Higher values create more dramatic temperature changes based on context entropy
• Controlled By: 'dynatemp' sampler (must be in samplers array and dynatemp_range > 0.0)

mirostat_tau.tooltip:
Mirostat Tau (Mirostat Sampler Parameter)
• Function: Target entropy level for Mirostat algorithm, controls desired text unpredictability
• Range: 1.0 to 10.0 (higher values = more diverse/unpredictable text)
• Server Default: 5.0
• Effects: Algorithm adjusts temperature to maintain this target entropy level
• Controlled By: 'mirostat' sampler (must be in samplers array and mirostat = 1 or 2)

mirostat_eta.tooltip:
Mirostat Eta (Mirostat Sampler Parameter)
• Function: Learning rate for Mirostat algorithm, controls how quickly it adapts to achieve target entropy
• Range: 0.01 to 1.0 (higher values = faster adaptation)
• Server Default: 0.1
• Effects: Higher values make quicker adjustments, lower values make gradual changes
• Controlled By: 'mirostat' sampler (must be in samplers array and mirostat = 1 or 2)

samplers.tooltip:
Sampler Sequence Control
• Function: Defines the exact order in which sampling algorithms are applied during token generation
• Range: Array of sampler names: temperature, top_k, top_p, min_p, typ_p, top_n_sigma, penalties, dry, xtc, mirostat, dynatemp
• Server Default: [\"penalties\", \"dry\", \"top_n_sigma\", \"top_k\", \"typ_p\", \"top_p\", \"min_p\", \"xtc\", \"temperature\"]
• Effects: Different sequences can significantly impact generation quality and behavior
• WARNING: Must use array format. Parameters not in sequence will be ignored regardless of their individual settings
• Independent Samplers: temperature, top_k, top_p, min_p, typ_p, top_n_sigma, penalties, dry, xtc, mirostat, dynatemp

max_tokens.tooltip:
Maximum Tokens
• Function: Maximum number of tokens to generate in the response
• Range: -2 to 8192 (-1 = unlimited, -2 = use server context size)
• Server Default: -1 (unlimited)
• Effects: Controls response length and prevents runaway generation

n_predict.tooltip:
N Predict (Alternative to max_tokens)
• Function: Alternative parameter name for maximum tokens to generate
• Range: -2 to 8192 (-1 = unlimited, -2 = use server context size)
• Server Default: -1 (unlimited)
• Effects: Identical to max_tokens, use one or the other, not both

n_keep.tooltip:
Keep Tokens
• Function: Number of tokens from the beginning of context to always keep during context shifting
• Range: 0 to 8192 (0 = keep none, -1 = keep all)
• Server Default: 0
• Effects: Preserves important prompt tokens when context becomes full, prevents losing key instructions

n_discard.tooltip:
Discard Tokens
• Function: Number of tokens to discard from the beginning when context shifting is needed
• Range: 0 to 8192 (0 = discard based on automatic calculation)
• Server Default: 0 (automatic)
• Effects: Controls which tokens are removed first during context management

min_keep.tooltip:
Minimum Keep Tokens
• Function: Minimum number of tokens that must be kept when discarding during context shifting
• Range: 0 to 8192 (0 = no minimum requirement)
• Server Default: 0
• Effects: Ensures critical prompt information is preserved even under memory pressure

seed.tooltip:
Random Seed
• Function: Random number generator seed for reproducible generation
• Range: -1 to 4294967295 (-1 = random seed)
• Server Default: -1 (random)
• Effects: Same seed with identical parameters produces identical outputs, essential for testing and benchmarking

stream.tooltip:
Streaming Response
• Function: Enable streaming response (tokens sent as generated rather than all at once)
• Range: true or false
• Server Default: false
• Effects: true enables real-time token streaming, false waits for complete response

stop.tooltip:
Stop Sequences
• Function: Array of strings that will stop generation when encountered
• Range: Array of strings (e.g., [\"\
\
\", \"END\", \"###\"])
• Server Default: [] (empty array)
• Effects: Provides precise control over when generation should terminate

model.tooltip:
Model Name
• Function: Specifies the model name for the API request (informational)
• Range: Any string (typically model identifier)
• Server Default: \"qwen-2.5-14b\"
• Effects: Usually ignored by llama.cpp server, model is determined by --model server parameter

logit_bias.tooltip:
Logit Bias
• Function: Modifies the probability of specific tokens by applying bias values to their logits before sampling
• Range: Object with token IDs as keys and bias values as numbers (e.g., {\"15043\": 1.0, \"12345\": -1.0})
• Server Default: {} (empty object)
• Effects: Positive values increase token probability, negative values decrease it, enabling fine control over vocabulary

ignore_eos.tooltip:
Ignore End-of-Stream
• Function: Continue generation even after encountering end-of-stream tokens
• Range: true or false
• Server Default: false
• Effects: true forces continued generation past natural stopping points, false respects EOS tokens
• WARNING: Can cause infinite generation - always set max_tokens when using this

n_probs.tooltip:
Number of Probabilities
• Function: Include the log probabilities of the top N most likely tokens in the response
• Range: 0 to 100 (0 = no probabilities returned)
• Server Default: 0
• Effects: Provides token probability information for analysis, debugging, or confidence assessment

grammar.tooltip:
Grammar Constraints
• Function: BNF-style grammar rules to constrain generation output format
• Range: String containing GBNF grammar rules (e.g., \"root ::= object\
object ::= '{' ws '}' | '{' ws pair (',' ws pair)* '}'\")
• Server Default: \"\" (no constraints)
• Effects: Forces generated text to conform to specified grammar structure, useful for structured output

grammar_lazy.tooltip:
Grammar Lazy Mode
• Function: Enable lazy evaluation of grammar constraints for potentially better performance
• Range: true or false
• Server Default: false
• Effects: May improve generation speed with complex grammars but could affect constraint enforcement
• WARNING: Only effective when grammar parameter is provided

grammar_triggers.tooltip:
Grammar Triggers
• Function: Array of strings that trigger grammar constraint activation during generation
• Range: Array of strings (e.g., [\"{\\
\", \"[\", \"START\"])
• Server Default: [] (empty array)
• Effects: Grammar constraints only apply after encountering one of these trigger strings
• WARNING: Only effective when grammar parameter is provided

preserved_tokens.tooltip:
Preserved Tokens
• Function: Array of token IDs that should be preserved and not subject to certain sampling constraints
• Range: Array of integer token IDs (e.g., [198, 220, 628])
• Server Default: [] (empty array)
• Effects: Specified tokens bypass certain sampling restrictions, useful for maintaining format tokens

json_schema.tooltip:
JSON Schema Constraints
• Function: JSON schema object that constrains generation to produce valid JSON matching the schema
• Range: Valid JSON schema object (e.g., {\"type\": \"object\", \"properties\": {...}})
• Server Default: null (no constraints)
• Effects: Ensures generated output conforms to specified JSON structure, perfect for structured data extraction

n.tooltip:
Number of Completions
• Function: Number of completion responses to generate for each input
• Range: 1 to 10
• Server Default: 1
• Effects: Higher values generate multiple different responses, useful for comparison or selection

logprobs.tooltip:
Log Probabilities
• Function: Include log probabilities of tokens in the response for OpenAI API compatibility
• Range: null or positive integer
• Server Default: null (no log probabilities)
• Effects: Provides token probability information for analysis and debugging

top_logprobs.tooltip:
Top Log Probabilities
• Function: Number of top alternative tokens to include with their log probabilities
• Range: null or positive integer
• Server Default: null
• Effects: Shows probability alternatives for each generated token, useful for understanding model confidence

echo.tooltip:
Echo Input
• Function: Include the input prompt in the response output
• Range: true or false
• Server Default: false
• Effects: true returns both prompt and completion, false returns only the completion

suffix.tooltip:
Completion Suffix
• Function: Text that should come after the generated completion (for infill tasks)
• Range: Any string or null
• Server Default: null
• Effects: Used for code completion and fill-in-the-middle tasks where context follows the generation

user.tooltip:
User Identifier
• Function: Unique identifier for the user making the request (OpenAI compatibility)
• Range: Any string or null
• Server Default: null
• Effects: Typically used for tracking and analytics, may not affect generation behavior

tools.tooltip:
Function Tools
• Function: Array of tool/function definitions available for the model to call during generation
• Range: Array of tool definition objects with function schemas
• Server Default: [] (no tools available)
• Effects: Enables function calling capabilities, allowing model to invoke external tools

tool_choice.tooltip:
Tool Choice Strategy
• Function: Controls how the model decides whether to use available tools
• Range: \"auto\" (model decides), \"none\" (never use tools), \"required\" (must use a tool)
• Server Default: \"auto\"
• Effects: Determines tool usage behavior and response format when tools are available
• WARNING: Only effective when tools array is provided

slot_id.tooltip:
Slot ID
• Function: Specific slot ID to use for this request in multi-slot server configurations
• Range: null or positive integer
• Server Default: null (automatic slot assignment)
• Effects: Forces request to use specific processing slot, useful for isolation or debugging

cache_prompt.tooltip:
Cache Prompt
• Function: Whether to cache the processed prompt for potential reuse
• Range: true or false
• Server Default: true
• Effects: false ensures deterministic behavior by preventing prompt caching, true improves performance
• WARNING: Set to false for reproducible benchmarking to avoid cache contamination

reasoning_in_content.tooltip:
Reasoning in Content
• Function: Include reasoning/thinking process in the main response content
• Range: true or false
• Server Default: false
• Effects: true shows model's reasoning process in output, false keeps only final response

thinking_forced_open.tooltip:
Thinking Forced Open
• Function: Force the model to show its thinking process even when it would normally hide it
• Range: true or false
• Server Default: false
• Effects: true makes internal reasoning visible, useful for understanding model decision-making

anti_prompt.tooltip:
Anti Prompt
• Function: Array of strings that will stop generation when encountered (alternative to stop sequences)
• Range: Array of strings
• Server Default: [] (empty array)
• Effects: Similar to stop parameter but processed differently by the server

assistant_name.tooltip:
Assistant Name
• Function: Name to use for the assistant in chat-style conversations
• Range: Any string or null
• Server Default: null (use default)
• Effects: Customizes assistant identity in chat templates, may influence response style

user_name.tooltip:
User Name
• Function: Name to use for the user in chat-style conversations
• Range: Any string or null
• Server Default: null (use default)
• Effects: Customizes user identity in chat templates, may influence how assistant addresses user

query.tooltip:
Reranking Query
• Function: Query string for document reranking operations
• Range: Any string or null
• Server Default: null
• Effects: Used to rank documents by relevance to this query string

documents.tooltip:
Documents for Reranking
• Function: Array of document strings to be ranked by relevance to the query
• Range: Array of strings
• Server Default: [] (empty array)
• Effects: Documents will be scored and ranked based on query relevance

input_prefix.tooltip:
Code Input Prefix
• Function: Code context that comes before the completion point (for code completion tasks)
• Range: Any string or null
• Server Default: null
• Effects: Provides context for fill-in-the-middle code completion, defines what comes before the cursor

input_suffix.tooltip:
Code Input Suffix
• Function: Code context that comes after the completion point (for code completion tasks)
• Range: Any string or null
• Server Default: null
• Effects: Provides context for fill-in-the-middle code completion, defines what comes after the cursor

input.tooltip:
Embedding Input
• Function: Text string to generate embeddings for
• Range: Any string or null
• Server Default: null
• Effects: Input text will be converted to vector embeddings for semantic analysis

encoding_format.tooltip:
Embedding Encoding Format
• Function: Format for returning embedding vectors
• Range: \"float\" (array of numbers) or \"base64\" (base64-encoded string)
• Server Default: \"float\"
• Effects: Determines how embedding data is encoded in the response

chat_template_kwargs.tooltip:
Chat Template Arguments (JSON Object)
• Function: Pass custom parameters to Jinja chat templates for model behavior control
• Format: JSON object with template-specific variables
• Primary Use: GPT-OSS models for reasoning effort control
• Examples:
  - {"reasoning_effort": "low"} - minimal thinking
  - {"reasoning_effort": "medium"} - balanced reasoning (default)
  - {"reasoning_effort": "high"} - maximum reasoning depth
• Usage: Enter valid JSON like: {"reasoning_effort": "low"}
• Technical: Parameters are passed to Jinja template renderer during chat formatting

response_fields.tooltip:
Response Fields
• Function: Array of specific fields to include in the response (advanced response control)
• Range: Array of field names
• Server Default: [] (include standard fields)
• Effects: Customizes response structure to include only specified fields
